notes: Primary constructor. Simply stores the two arguments into aString2985/anInt2987, wrapped in a try/catch that rethrows any RuntimeException as TextureLoadException with a formatted 'sj.<init>(...)' arg dump (a decompiler/obfuscator artifact common to many constructors in this codebase, not real logic). Only four instances are ever constructed in the whole repo, each a static singleton keyed by a brand/environment name and a small ordinal id: ParticleEmitterNode.aSceneProjector_186 = SceneProjector("runescape", 0), GlRectangleTexture.aSceneProjector_8638 = SceneProjector("stellardawn", 1), GlslEnvMaterialPass.aSceneProjector_6262 = SceneProjector("game3", 2), CustomCursorsOptionState.aSceneProjector_5932 = SceneProjector("game4", 3). Client.aSceneProjector_10434 holds the currently-selected one and is compared by reference throughout the client (Client.kt, CollisionMap.kt, NativeIndexBuffer.kt, SpriteDefinition.kt, WaterMaterialPass.kt, ParticleEmitterListNode.kt) to branch on 'which game/brand build is this' -- e.g. GlslEnvMaterialPass.kt builds a URL as "http://"+string+"."+aString2985+".com/..." using the name field as a subdomain, and anInt2987 (id) is used as a direct array index (SocketFactory.anIntArray3475!![...anInt2987]) and written to the network stream (ColourAdjustment.kt, SceneNodeDeque.kt). Despite the class name (carried over from the source deobfuscation pass and not to be changed here), the runtime role is closer to a 'game build/environment descriptor' than a scene projector; only the constructor parameter names are being proposed here.

Override of kotlin.Any.toString() -- name cannot be changed since it satisfies the Any contract. Body unconditionally increments the companion counter anInt2989 then throws IllegalStateException() with no message, meaning any accidental string-concatenation or logging of a SceneProjector instance would crash. No call site anywhere in the repo actually invokes toString() or relies on string interpolation of a SceneProjector value (all real usages read aString2985/anInt2987 directly, e.g. Client.kt:1392/2008, GlslEnvMaterialPass.kt:148). anInt2989 is reset to 0 once per frame in FrameStatsReset.kt:3575 alongside the other per-frame diagnostic counters in this codebase, even though the throw would make repeated increments within a frame impossible in practice -- consistent with this being a stubbed-out/'should never be called' guard method preserved from decompilation rather than functional code.
